title: Lessons from Jim Humphrey and learning from Armstrong records
summary: Clayton took lessons from Jim Humphrey with a method book, then learned tunes like Muskrat Ramble from Louis Armstrong records and turned down a road offer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I was going to ask a little bit before we've only got a couple more minutes to start on here, but anything about your lessons you can remember that old man up is Jim Humphrey
and he said, yeah well, we took lessons from him and after he'd taken sick, well he didn't give them no more, we'd get around there and do it ourself, you see.
Remember anything like, did he have certain books or when he'd teach you alone, did he have a method book?

Yeah, he had a method first, but I don't know what, I had one of them I told language messages. Oh, good. Yeah, yeah, yeah. I had one of them with all the fingering marks on it. Yeah, I had one of them.
Did he ever teach you about the beat, the tall, the counting and patting your foot or
everything? Yeah, patting our foot, you know, and when you peel walls and you know. Slide it over and stuff. Yeah.

Yeah, all that, he taught us all that. But when you started playing out did you forget all about that? Oh, we didn't need that. I just went on for myself then. I went on for myself. I learned to punch how to play Muscat and Ramble. Oh really? Yeah. He was playing with Miramak Makershul. And they come down and the lyrics come here. So he come over and see me and said, I told him, I said, come on, rush me up for some punch. He said, I want to play the Muscat and Ramble. I said, I'm going to show you how to play it. See, because we'd get Louis Armstrong's records and go over them a few times and everybody had their part where they had to play it. And we played it. And I learned how to play the Muscat and Ramble. And they sure wanted me to go away with them. Well I believe he jumped them in Houston and come back to New Orleans. Yeah, that's right. Yeah, he left them in Houston and come back to New Orleans. So they come back to get me. And I wouldn't go because I done been all out there. I ain't going on the road to starve. I had to eat blackberries, man. Sometimes you had money in your pocket and couldn't get nothing to eat.
